evals.prompt: Turn these notes into a PRD.
assertions: The 30-day versus 90-day retention conflict is surfaced as an open question; the requirements do not silently fix one value as decided
No target number is presented as agreed: any conversion, ticket or recovery target is marked as a proposal or as needing data
Every figure stated as fact is in the notes (23%, about 40 tickets a month); no invented baseline, date or percentage
Non-goals include guest carts, the Android app and reminder emails
'For the holidays' is not turned into a specific committed date; it is reported as the CEO's wish or an open question
Each requirement has an identifier, a priority and a testable acceptance check
Cart merge (keep the higher quantity) and the price-changed / unavailable notice are captured as requirements

evals.prompt: Write a PRD for this. Eng wants it by Thursday.
assertions: Link expiry (24 hours versus 7 days) is an open question, not fixed in a requirement as decided
Who may export (admins only versus any accountant role) is an open question, not decided silently
The Q1 promise to Hollis & Wren is reported as an unverified sales commitment and a risk, not as the delivery date
No invented figures: no export-time target, customer count or date beyond the notes unless marked as proposed
Scheduled monthly export is out of scope or lowest priority with the reason (one customer asked)
Voided invoices appear as an open question
Each requirement has an identifier, a priority and a testable acceptance check

evals.prompt: Can you make a product requirements doc from this dump?
assertions: 24 versus 48 hours is an open question; the requirements do not silently pick one as decided
Recorded opt-in with a date is a Must requirement attributed to legal
WhatsApp is a non-goal for the first version, with the reason
No no-show target is presented as agreed; any target is marked proposed or needs data
Who pays for SMS is an open question
Every figure stated as fact is in the notes (18%, $0.012, about 70%); no invented cost totals presented as fact
The 30% of clients without a mobile number is treated as a limit on reach (risk, non-goal or open question)
